title: Science Monopoly
theme: Build your science empire by funding labs, discovering breakthroughs, and winning Nobel Prizes.
description: Step into the world of scientific discovery in this Monopoly-inspired board game! Fund research labs, publish groundbreaking papers, navigate funding cuts, and outsmart rival scientists. Invest in physics, biology, chemistry, and cutting-edge technology as you race to build the ultimate science empire. Every decision teaches real scientific thinking — from hypothesis testing to knowing when to pivot your research.

storybook_pages.title: Welcome to Science Monopoly
storybook_pages.text: You are a brilliant young scientist with a ₹80L research grant and a dream to change the world. The frontier of discovery awaits — fund labs, publish breakthroughs, and build your science empire!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: colorful monopoly board game with science labs, microscopes, atoms, test tubes, beakers, Nobel Prize medal, cartoon style, vibrant

storybook_pages.title: The Research Board
storybook_pages.text: Roll the dice and move around the board. Land on research fields to fund them. When rivals use your labs, they pay you licensing fees!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: game board with colorful science tiles, dice rolling, game pieces shaped like atoms and rockets, laboratory buildings, cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Build Your Science Empire
storybook_pages.text: Upgrade your labs with better equipment to attract top researchers. Collect sets of related disciplines for synergy bonuses. Watch out for Funding Cuts and Ethics Review tiles!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: growing science empire, laboratories getting bigger, Nobel Prize ceremony, space rockets launching, DNA helix glowing, cartoon style

how_to_play: Roll the dice and move around the 28-tile board. Each lap earns you $20K in renewed grant funding.
Land on an unowned research field? Fund it to start collecting licensing fees when others use your lab.
Own all labs in a discipline group to double your licensing revenue from that set.
Use the Equipment Shop tile to upgrade your labs — upgrades increase the fees rivals pay you.
Watch out for Ethics Review tiles (you lose funding) and Equipment Failure events (random setbacks).
Discovery tiles give random bonuses or penalties — just like real research!
First player to reach $500K total valuation (grants + lab values) wins. Or outlast all rivals to claim the Nobel Prize!

challenge.fail_message: Not quite right. The committee passes on your nomination, and it costs you $5K in conference fees. 😓

ai_competitors.name: Dr. Reckless

ai_competitors.name: Professor Steady

evt_physics_lab.title: Physics Lab — Quantum Dynamics Institute
evt_physics_lab.story: A cutting-edge physics lab is seeking a primary funder. They are on the verge of confirming a new subatomic particle. Equipment is top-notch and the lead researcher studied under a Nobel laureate.

choices.label: Fund fully for $25K — particle physics is fundamental!
choices.feedback: The Quantum Dynamics Institute is now under your patronage! They generate $5K per cycle in licensing fees from their discoveries. ⚛️

choices.label: Co-fund for $12K — share the risk with another patron
choices.feedback: You split funding with another patron. $2.5K per cycle, but your exposure is limited. Smart hedging!

choices.label: Pass — fundamental research takes too long to pay off
choices.feedback: You pass on physics. Basic research can take decades to yield applications, but Einstein started there...

evt_chemistry_lab.title: Chemistry Lab — MolecuTech Solutions
evt_chemistry_lab.story: A chemistry lab has synthesized a new polymer with extraordinary heat resistance. Industrial applications are enormous — aerospace, electronics, and automotive companies are interested.

choices.label: Invest $30K — patentable materials are goldmines!
choices.feedback: MolecuTech's heat-resistant polymer gets patented! $6K per cycle from aerospace licensing deals. 🧪

choices.label: Offer $15K for exclusive licensing rights only
choices.feedback: You secure licensing rights without full ownership. $3.5K per cycle — lower cost, decent returns.

choices.label: Pass — materials science is too niche for me
choices.feedback: You pass on chemistry. Some of the biggest fortunes were built on patented materials, though.

evt_biology_research.title: Biology Research — BioVita Labs
evt_biology_research.story: A biology team has identified a protein that could slow cellular aging. They need $28K for clinical trials. If it works, it could revolutionize medicine.

choices.label: Fund $28K — anti-aging research is a trillion-dollar market!
choices.feedback: BioVita's clinical trials show promise! You earn $5.5K per cycle from pharma licensing. 🧬

choices.label: Invest $14K for a smaller stake in the trial
choices.feedback: Smaller investment in a high-potential field. $3K per cycle with less downside if trials fail.

choices.label: Too risky — clinical trials fail 90% of the time
choices.feedback: You pass. Clinical trial failure rates are brutal. But the 10% that succeed change the world.

evt_space_program.title: Space Program — Orbital Dynamics Corp
evt_space_program.story: A private space company is developing reusable micro-satellites for Earth observation. They need $40K for their first orbital launch. Government contracts are already lined up.

choices.label: All in! $40K — space is the ultimate frontier!
choices.feedback: Orbital Dynamics launches successfully! Government contracts bring $8K per cycle. You are reaching for the stars! 🚀

choices.label: Invest $20K via milestone-based funding
choices.feedback: Milestone funding means you pay as they prove themselves. $4K per cycle with built-in risk management.

choices.label: Pass — rockets blow up too often for my taste
choices.feedback: You skip space. Rockets do explode sometimes... but SpaceX proved the model works.

evt_robotics_lab.title: Robotics Lab — AutoMech Industries
evt_robotics_lab.story: A robotics lab has built a surgical robot prototype with 10x better precision than human surgeons. Hospitals are lining up for demos. They need $22K for FDA testing.

choices.label: Invest $22K — surgical robots are the future!
choices.feedback: AutoMech's surgical robot passes FDA trials! $5K per cycle from hospital licensing fees. 🤖

choices.label: Offer $12K for a revenue share on each unit sold
choices.feedback: Revenue share means you earn per robot sold. $3.5K per cycle with scalable upside.

choices.label: FDA approval is uncertain — too risky
choices.feedback: You skip robotics. FDA approval is a gauntlet, but medical devices have enormous margins.

evt_ai_research.title: AI Research Center — DeepMind Institute
evt_ai_research.story: An AI research center is building neural networks that can predict protein structures. This could revolutionize drug discovery. They need $45K for GPU clusters and talent.

choices.label: Go big! $45K — AI-driven science will change everything!
choices.feedback: The AI Research Center predicts 200 new protein structures! $10K per cycle from pharma partnerships. This is transformative! 🧠

choices.label: Invest $20K via convertible grant — be cautious
choices.feedback: Convertible grant means lower risk. $4K per cycle now, with upside if they publish in Nature.

choices.label: AI hype is overblown — pass on this one
choices.feedback: You skip AI research. The field IS competitive, but the winners will reshape science entirely.

evt_genetics_lab.title: Genetics Lab — GenomeX Therapeutics
evt_genetics_lab.story: A CRISPR gene-editing lab has developed a technique to correct sickle cell disease. Human trials await. They need $35K for regulatory approval and patient recruitment.

choices.label: Invest $35K — gene therapy is the next medical revolution!
choices.feedback: GenomeX receives breakthrough therapy designation! $7K per cycle from treatment licensing. This could save millions of lives. 🧬

choices.label: Invest $15K — hedge against regulatory risk
choices.feedback: Conservative play on gene therapy. $3K per cycle. If regulations shift, you are less exposed.

choices.label: Gene editing ethics concern me — I will wait
choices.feedback: You wait on the sidelines. CRISPR ethics are complex, but the technology marches forward.

evt_marine_biology.title: Marine Biology — OceanDeep Research
evt_marine_biology.story: A marine biology team has discovered deep-sea organisms producing compounds that kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria. They need $20K for a research vessel expedition.

choices.label: Fund the expedition for $20K — the ocean holds untold secrets!
choices.feedback: OceanDeep discovers 3 new antibiotic compounds! $4K per cycle from pharmaceutical licensing. 🐋

choices.label: Offer $10K plus your network contacts in pharma
choices.feedback: Your pharma connections accelerate their research. $3K per cycle plus reputation boost.

choices.label: Expeditions are expensive and uncertain — pass
choices.feedback: You skip marine biology. Expeditions are pricey, but the ocean covers 71% of Earth and remains mostly unexplored.

evt_nuclear_energy.title: Nuclear Energy — FusionCore Labs
evt_nuclear_energy.story: A nuclear fusion startup claims they are 5 years from a working prototype. Their tokamak design is novel and backed by university physicists. They need $38K for superconducting magnets.

choices.label: Invest $38K — fusion energy would change civilization!
choices.feedback: FusionCore achieves stable plasma containment! $7.5K per cycle from energy company partnerships. The holy grail of energy is closer! ☢️

choices.label: Invest $18K — fusion is always 20 years away, right?
choices.feedback: Modest fusion bet. $3.5K per cycle. If they crack it, you are early. If not, you survive.

choices.label: Fusion is a money pit — always 20 years away
choices.feedback: You pass on fusion. Skeptics have said this for decades — but recent breakthroughs suggest they may finally be wrong.

evt_quantum_computing.title: Quantum Computing — QubitForge
evt_quantum_computing.story: A quantum computing lab has achieved 1,000-qubit stability at near absolute zero. Pharmaceutical companies want to use it for drug simulation. They need $42K for cryogenic infrastructure.

choices.label: Invest $42K — quantum supremacy is within reach!
choices.feedback: QubitForge demonstrates quantum advantage in drug simulation! $9K per cycle from compute-time licensing. The quantum era begins! 💻

choices.label: Invest $20K for limited compute-time access
choices.feedback: Limited investment, but you secure priority access. $4.5K per cycle from sublicensing.

choices.label: Quantum is too experimental — classical computers still win
choices.feedback: You pass on quantum. Classical computers are proven, but quantum could solve problems they never will.

evt_nanotechnology.title: Nanotechnology — NanoScale Dynamics
evt_nanotechnology.story: A nanotech lab has created self-assembling nanoparticles that can deliver drugs directly to cancer cells, reducing side effects by 80%. They need $25K for animal trials.

choices.label: Invest $25K — targeted drug delivery is revolutionary!
choices.feedback: NanoScale's nanoparticles show 90% tumor reduction in trials! $5K per cycle from oncology partnerships. 🔬

choices.label: Invest $12K — nanotech is promising but early-stage
choices.feedback: Modest nanotech investment. $2.5K per cycle. If the trials succeed, you can invest more later.

choices.label: Pass — too many nanotech promises, too few products
choices.feedback: You skip nanotech. The field has overpromised before, but the science is finally catching up.

evt_environmental_science.title: Environmental Science — TerraWatch Analytics
evt_environmental_science.story: An environmental science team has built AI-powered satellite monitoring that can predict deforestation 6 months in advance. Governments and NGOs are interested. They need $22K for more satellite data.

choices.label: Invest $22K — saving the planet AND making money!
choices.feedback: TerraWatch signs contracts with 5 governments! $4.5K per cycle from monitoring subscriptions. Science for good! 🌍

choices.label: Offer $10K plus access to your data analytics team
choices.feedback: Your analytics expertise makes their models better. $3K per cycle plus enhanced reputation.

choices.label: Environmental monitoring does not monetize well — pass
choices.feedback: You pass on environmental science. Carbon credits and ESG mandates may prove you wrong soon.

evt_neuroscience.title: Neuroscience — BrainMap Institute
evt_neuroscience.story: A neuroscience lab has developed a non-invasive brain-computer interface that lets paralyzed patients control prosthetic limbs with thought alone. They need $32K for expanded clinical trials.

choices.label: Invest $32K — brain-computer interfaces will transform healthcare!
choices.feedback: BrainMap's BCI restores mobility to 15 patients in trials! $6.5K per cycle from medical device licensing. Incredible science! 🧠

choices.label: Invest $15K — incredible tech, but FDA is unpredictable
choices.feedback: Hedged bet on BCI technology. $3K per cycle with a seat on the advisory board.

choices.label: BCI is decades from mainstream — pass for now
choices.feedback: You pass on brain-computer interfaces. Neuralink and others disagree with your timeline.

evt_renewable_energy.title: Renewable Energy — SolarCell Innovations
evt_renewable_energy.story: A materials science team has created perovskite solar cells with 35% efficiency — nearly double current commercial panels. Manufacturing costs are low. They need $30K to build a pilot factory.

choices.label: Invest $30K — high-efficiency solar changes everything!
choices.feedback: SolarCell's pilot factory produces panels at half the cost of competitors! $6K per cycle from energy company orders. 🌱

choices.label: Invest $15K — dip your toes in clean energy
choices.feedback: Modest solar investment. $3K per cycle. Good for the planet and your portfolio.

choices.label: Solar panel margins are razor thin — hard pass
choices.feedback: You skip solar. Traditional margins are thin, but perovskite could be a game-changer.

evt_pharmaceutical.title: Pharmaceutical Company — CureGen Biopharma
evt_pharmaceutical.story: A pharmaceutical startup has a mRNA-based vaccine platform that can be adapted to any new virus in 48 hours. After the pandemic, governments want rapid-response vaccine capability. They need $35K.

choices.label: Invest $35K — pandemic preparedness is essential!
choices.feedback: CureGen signs government preparedness contracts! $7K per cycle from stockpile agreements. Science protecting humanity! 💊

choices.label: Invest $18K — pharma is regulated but high-margin
choices.feedback: Conservative pharma play. $3.5K per cycle. Regulated industries reward patience.

choices.label: Pharma regulation is a nightmare — not for me
choices.feedback: You skip pharma. The regulatory maze is real, but the margins for those who navigate it are extraordinary.

evt_chance_1.title: Discovery Card!
evt_chance_1.story: Your research team publishes in Nature! The paper goes viral in the scientific community, attracting attention from funding agencies worldwide.

choices.label: Accept all the conference invitations and media interviews
choices.feedback: The publicity brings $10K in new grant money and your reputation soars in the scientific community! 📰

choices.label: Stay in the lab — the next discovery will not find itself
choices.feedback: You skip the spotlight and focus on research. Your next paper is even more groundbreaking.

evt_chance_2.title: Discovery Card!
evt_chance_2.story: A rival lab just lost their funding! Their top researchers are looking for new positions and their equipment is being auctioned.

choices.label: Spend $15K to hire their researchers and buy equipment
choices.feedback: Brilliant! You acquire world-class talent and equipment at a discount. $5K boost to revenue. 🎯

choices.label: Let talent come to you naturally — save your grant money
choices.feedback: Some researchers apply on their own. Fewer than you hoped, but it cost nothing extra.

evt_chance_3.title: Discovery Card!
evt_chance_3.story: Your main experimental apparatus breaks down during a critical experiment! Months of data could be lost.

choices.label: Pay $20K for emergency repair and data recovery
choices.feedback: Emergency repairs save the data! Your experiment continues and the results are published on schedule. 🛡️

choices.label: Patch it yourself and hope the data survived
choices.feedback: You pull all-nighters fixing equipment. Some data was corrupted, but most survived. Close call!

evt_chance_4.title: Discovery Card!
evt_chance_4.story: You receive an urgent call: a prestigious international science foundation wants to award your lab a $50K unrestricted research grant. But you must present your work in Geneva within 48 hours.

choices.label: Book the flight and prepare the presentation overnight
choices.feedback: You win the international grant! $50K in funding and your name is known worldwide! 🏆

choices.label: Too short notice — I cannot prepare a worthy presentation
choices.feedback: You pass on the trip. Rest matters, but was a $50K grant and global recognition worth one sleepless night? Probably.

glossary_terms.definition: Funding awarded by governments, foundations, or corporations to support scientific research. Grants are typically non-repayable but require published results.
glossary_terms.example: The National Science Foundation awards a $500K grant to a university lab studying climate change.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: A grant is free money for science — but you must deliver results and publish your findings.

glossary_terms.definition: The process where other experts in your field evaluate your research before it gets published. It helps ensure scientific quality and catches errors.
glossary_terms.example: Before publishing in Nature, your paper is reviewed by 3 anonymous scientists who check your methods and conclusions.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Peer review = other scientists checking your homework before the world sees it.

glossary_terms.definition: A legal right that gives an inventor exclusive control over their invention for typically 20 years. Others must pay to use your patented technology.
glossary_terms.example: CRISPR gene-editing technology generated billions in patent licensing fees for the universities that developed it.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: A patent is a 20-year monopoly on your invention. It turns discoveries into dollars.

glossary_terms.definition: A carefully controlled experiment testing new medical treatments on humans. Trials progress through phases (I, II, III) before a treatment can be approved.
glossary_terms.example: Phase III clinical trials for a new cancer drug involved 10,000 patients across 50 hospitals over 3 years.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Clinical trials = the long, expensive road from lab bench to medicine cabinet.

glossary_terms.definition: A testable prediction about how something works. The foundation of the scientific method — you propose an idea, then design experiments to prove or disprove it.
glossary_terms.example: Hypothesis: Plants grow faster under blue light. Experiment: Grow identical plants under blue, red, and white light for 30 days.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: A hypothesis is an educated guess that you can test. No test = no science.

glossary_terms.definition: A revolutionary gene-editing tool that lets scientists precisely cut and modify DNA. Like molecular scissors that can edit the code of life itself.
glossary_terms.example: Scientists used CRISPR to remove the gene causing sickle cell disease in patient blood cells, potentially curing the condition.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: CRISPR = genetic scissors. Cut, paste, and edit DNA like editing a document.

glossary_terms.definition: The point at which a quantum computer can solve a problem that no classical computer could solve in a reasonable time. A major milestone in computing.
glossary_terms.example: Google claimed quantum supremacy when their Sycamore processor solved in 200 seconds what would take a supercomputer 10,000 years.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Quantum supremacy = the moment quantum computers outrun every regular computer on Earth.

glossary_terms.definition: The most prestigious award in science, given annually for outstanding contributions in Physics, Chemistry, Physiology/Medicine, and other fields. Established by Alfred Nobel in 1895.
glossary_terms.example: The 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier for developing CRISPR gene editing.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: The Nobel Prize is the ultimate science trophy — fewer than 1,000 people have ever won one.

win_conditions.description: Race around the board funding labs, collecting licensing revenue, and building your science empire. Reach the Nobel Prize tile or achieve the highest net worth to win!

scientific_method.definition: A systematic approach to investigation: observe, hypothesize, experiment, analyze, conclude. The foundation of all scientific discovery.
scientific_method.example: Noticing plants grow toward light, hypothesizing they need light, testing by growing plants in dark vs light.
scientific_method.real_world_example: COVID-19 vaccines were developed using rigorous scientific method — from hypothesis to clinical trials in record time.

hypothesis.definition: A testable prediction about the relationship between variables. A good hypothesis can be proven wrong.
hypothesis.example: "If I water plants with salt water, they will grow slower than plants watered with fresh water."
hypothesis.real_world_example: Einstein hypothesized that gravity bends light — confirmed during a 1919 solar eclipse, revolutionizing physics.

peer_review.definition: The process where other scientists evaluate research before publication to ensure quality, accuracy, and validity.
peer_review.example: Before publishing a study on a new drug, other pharmacologists review the methodology and data.
peer_review.real_world_example: The journal Nature receives over 10,000 submissions per year — only 8% survive peer review.

control_variable.definition: A variable kept constant during an experiment to ensure that any observed effect is due to the variable being tested.
control_variable.example: When testing fertilizer effects on plant growth, keeping water, sunlight, and soil type the same.
control_variable.real_world_example: In clinical drug trials, the placebo group serves as the control — they receive a fake treatment.

empirical_evidence.definition: Knowledge acquired through observation and experimentation, as opposed to theory or pure logic.
empirical_evidence.example: Measuring the temperature at which water boils at sea level (100°C) rather than calculating it theoretically.
empirical_evidence.real_world_example: Charles Darwin gathered empirical evidence across decades of observation before publishing On the Origin of Species.

innovation.definition: Applying scientific knowledge to create new technologies, processes, or solutions that improve human life.
innovation.example: Using knowledge of electromagnetism to invent wireless charging for phones.
innovation.real_world_example: CRISPR gene editing technology emerged from studying how bacteria defend against viruses — now it can cure genetic diseases.

coaching_moment: Step into the world of scientific discovery in this Monopoly-inspired board game! Fund research labs, publish groundbreaking papers, navigate funding cuts, and outsmart rival scientists.
cultural_context: Science literacy is a strategic national priority in India, with NEP 2020 emphasising inquiry-based learning over rote memorisation. Making science engaging through game-based formats accelerates this pedagogical shift.
reflection_prompt: Which turn was your turning point — and was it skill, luck, or planning?
